concepts.name: Bengaluru as India's Silicon Valley: Origins and Dominance
key_dimensions: Historical role of ISRO, HAL, and DRDO as catalysts for IT ecosystem
Why Bengaluru leads over other cities — skilled workforce, climate, IISC proximity
Key MNCs and Indian IT giants headquartered here vs. other clusters
UPSC trap: Distinguishing 'first IT cluster' vs. 'largest IT cluster' narratives

concepts.name: STPI (Software Technology Parks of India): Structure and Role in IT Clusters
key_dimensions: Establishment year (1991), parent ministry (MeitY), and statutory vs. non-statutory status
100% export-oriented unit status and tax exemption history (Section 10A of Income Tax Act)
STPI nodes across India — which cities have STPI and which rely on SEZs instead
UPSC trap: Difference between STPI scheme benefits vs. SEZ benefits for IT companies

concepts.name: IT SEZs vs. STPI: Overlap, Distinction, and Policy Shift
key_dimensions: SEZ Act 2005 and how IT SEZs differ from STPI in terms of infrastructure and tax treatment
Sunset clause on STPI tax benefits (ended 2011) and migration of units to SEZs
Geographic concentration of IT SEZs — Hyderabad HITEC City, Pune, Chennai corridors
UPSC trap: IT companies can operate under both STPI and SEZ simultaneously — false or true?

concepts.name: Hyderabad's HITEC City: Planned IT Cluster Model
key_dimensions: Role of Chandrababu Naidu's policy vision and public-private partnership model
HUDA Techno Enclave and Cyberabad Development Authority as governing bodies
Why Hyderabad is preferred by pharma-IT convergence companies (bioinformatics cluster)
UPSC trap: Cyberabad ≠ Hyderabad city — Cyberabad is a separate IT township/jurisdiction

concepts.name: Chennai IT Corridor: Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) Cluster
key_dimensions: OMR as India's first planned IT corridor — linear cluster model vs. hub model
Role of Tamil Nadu government's TIDEL Park as anchor institution
BPO and IT-ITeS dominance in Chennai vs. pure software development in Bengaluru
UPSC trap: Chennai ranks high in IT exports but is less associated with 'product companies'

concepts.name: Pune IT Cluster: Educational-Industrial Linkage Model
key_dimensions: Role of proximity to Mumbai financial hub and Symbiosis/COEP engineering colleges
Hinjewadi IT Park as Maharashtra's answer to HITEC City — MIDC's role
Automotive-IT convergence in Pune — embedded systems and ADAS development
UPSC trap: Pune is often confused with Mumbai for IT — Maharashtra's IT exports are largely from Pune, not Mumbai

concepts.name: NCR (Noida/Gurgaon) IT Cluster: Capital Proximity Advantage
key_dimensions: Gurgaon as BPO/ITES capital vs. Noida as software development hub — distinction
Role of DLF Cyber City (Gurgaon) and NSEZ Noida as anchor zones
Why NCR attracts global captive centers (GCCs) more than pure IT outsourcing firms
UPSC trap: NCR IT cluster spans two states (Haryana + UP) — governance complexity

concepts.name: Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in Indian IT Clusters
key_dimensions: Definition: GCCs are captive offshore units of MNCs — not outsourcing but insourcing
India hosts 50%+ of world's GCCs — Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune as top GCC cities
GCC vs. traditional IT outsourcing model — value chain position and employment quality
UPSC trap: GCCs are NOT the same as IT SEZs — GCCs are a business model, SEZs are a policy zone

concepts.name: Tier-2 IT Cities: Emerging Clusters and Government Push
key_dimensions: Cities like Coimbatore, Kochi, Jaipur, Indore, Bhubaneswar emerging as IT hubs
NASSCOM's 10,000 Startups and BPO Promotion Scheme targeting tier-2/3 cities
Cost arbitrage advantage of tier-2 cities vs. saturation in tier-1 clusters
UPSC trap: 'Kochi Smart City' project (UAE investment) vs. Kochi organic IT growth — different initiatives

concepts.name: NASSCOM: Role in IT Cluster Policy and Industry Advocacy
key_dimensions: NASSCOM as a non-statutory, industry body — NOT a government organization
NASSCOM's India Leadership Forum and its role in IT cluster promotion data
NASSCOM FutureSkills initiative and its linkage to cluster workforce development
UPSC trap: NASSCOM is NOT under MeitY control — it's an independent industry association

concepts.name: IT Industry Concentration and Regional Imbalance
key_dimensions: Top 5 cities account for 90%+ of India's IT exports — geographic concentration problem
Southern states (Karnataka, TN, Telangana, AP) dominate — North-South IT divide
Policy interventions: Digital India, BPO promotion scheme for North-East and J&K
UPSC trap: IT employment ≠ IT exports share — some states have high employment but low export value

concepts.name: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and IT Cluster Development: Legal Framework
key_dimensions: SEZ Act 2005: Sections relevant to IT/ITeS — single-window clearance, duty exemptions
Minimum area requirement for IT SEZs (10 hectares) vs. multi-product SEZs (1000 hectares)
Board of Approval (BoA) under Commerce Ministry — role in IT SEZ approvals
UPSC trap: IT SEZs have LOWER minimum area requirements than manufacturing SEZs — frequently tested

concepts.name: India's IT Export Geography: Which States Lead and Why
key_dimensions: Karnataka (~38%), Telangana (~17%), Tamil Nadu (~13%) — approximate share hierarchy
Role of state IT policies — Karnataka IT policy, Telangana TS-iPASS in attracting investment
Linkage between IIT/NIT locations and IT cluster emergence in nearby cities
UPSC trap: Maharashtra has large IT industry but ranks lower in IT exports due to domestic-focus firms

concepts.name: Start-up Ecosystem within IT Clusters: DPIIT Recognition and Hub Cities
key_dimensions: Bengaluru as 3rd largest start-up ecosystem globally — unicorn concentration data
T-Hub (Hyderabad), NASSCOM CoE, and Startup India Hubs as cluster-specific incubators
Distinction between IT start-ups (product) vs. IT services companies in cluster composition
UPSC trap: T-Hub is a Telangana state government initiative, NOT a central government body

concepts.name: Telecom and Digital Infrastructure as Prerequisite for IT Clusters
key_dimensions: Submarine cable landing stations — Chennai and Mumbai as primary gateways for IT connectivity
National Knowledge Network (NKN) connecting research institutions to IT ecosystem
Data center clustering near IT hubs — why Mumbai leads in data centers despite lower IT exports
UPSC trap: Data center hubs ≠ IT software export hubs — Mumbai leads former, Bengaluru latter

concepts.name: IT Industry Employment Patterns and Skill Geography
key_dimensions: Direct vs. indirect employment multiplier — IT sector's 1:4 indirect employment ratio
Gender participation in IT — higher female workforce % in IT vs. manufacturing sectors
Reverse migration trend: COVID-19 accelerating distributed IT work from tier-2 towns
UPSC trap: IT sector employs ~5 million directly but contributes ~8% of GDP — high productivity per worker

concepts.name: Electronics Manufacturing Clusters vs. IT Software Clusters: Convergence and Distinction
key_dimensions: EMC (Electronics Manufacturing Clusters) scheme under MeitY vs. STPI for software
Cities where both co-exist: Bengaluru (aerospace electronics + IT), Pune (auto electronics + IT)
PLI scheme for electronics vs. SEZ/STPI benefits for software — policy instrument difference
UPSC trap: Hardware manufacturing cluster ≠ IT software cluster — UPSC often conflates the two

concepts.name: IT Cluster Governance: Role of State IT Departments and Development Authorities
key_dimensions: Cyberabad Development Authority (Hyderabad), ELCOT (Tamil Nadu), KEONICS (Karnataka) as state nodal agencies
Single-window clearance systems at state level for IT parks — competitive federalism in IT
Urban local bodies vs. development authorities — jurisdictional conflicts in IT corridor governance
UPSC trap: ELCOT is Tamil Nadu's IT promotion agency but it also manages procurement — dual role

concepts.name: India's IT Clusters in Global Value Chain: Outsourcing to Innovation Transition
key_dimensions: Shift from BFSI outsourcing (1990s-2000s) to AI/cloud/cybersecurity (2010s-present) in cluster specialization
Bengaluru's R&D centre concentration vs. Chennai's BPO concentration — intra-India GVC hierarchy
UPSC trap: India's IT clusters are moving UP the value chain — but still largely services, not products
Comparison with competing clusters: Shenzhen (hardware), Dublin (European HQ), Singapore (APAC HQ)

concepts.name: COVID-19 Impact and Work-from-Home: Structural Change in IT Cluster Relevance
key_dimensions: OSP (Other Service Provider) regulations relaxed during COVID — allowed home-based IT work legally
Impact on commercial real estate in IT clusters — vacancy rates in HITEC City, OMR post-COVID
Emergence of 'distributed delivery model' and its threat to cluster-centric IT industry geography
UPSC trap: OSP regulations are under DoT (Telecom), not MeitY — inter-ministry jurisdiction point
